text:
**Riverbend scraps library late fees from 1 December**

- In a vote of 7-2, council has agreed to end overdue fines on books, magazines and DVDs at all five libraries across the district.
- Existing fines, which total about $38,000 across 6,400 members, will be wiped in full. Cards that were blocked only because of fines will unblock automatically on 1 December, and members will be emailed about this change in November.
- **Exceptions:** Lost or damaged items, or items not returned within 60 days, will still incur replacement cost and a blocked account. Inter-library loans will continue to keep lending councils' late fees, as they do now.
- **Rationale:** Council's reasoning is that fines deterred families, especially children, from using the libraries. It is also worth noting that other councils saw more returns after dropping their own fines.
- **Cost:** The change means about $52,000 in annual revenue is lost. This is partly offset by $19,000 previously spent chasing payments, which brings the net cost to about $33,000. One opposing councillor raised rates pressure as a concern.
- To make sure the policy is working as intended, it will be reviewed in 12 months.
